questions.questionText: Following a period of unusually cold weather, growers find that many of their tomato plants have been destroyed, reducing the supply of tomatoes. As a result of this
options: the price of tomatoes falls due to the signalling function of prices.
the price of tomatoes rises due to the rationing function of prices.
the quantity of tomatoes demanded rises due to the incentive function of prices.
the supply of tomatoes will fall further due to the signalling function of prices.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a function of prices in a market economy?
options: Allocating resources to the production of public goods
Ensuring that the distribution of goods and services is fair
Incentivising firms to produce the goods consumers want
Providing a measurement of positive and negative externalities

questions.questionText: Technological change has made it easier to charge for road use, including charging road users different prices according to demand at different times of the day. Which one of the following would be the most likely outcome if the government introduced variable charges, according to the time of day, for using motorways in the UK?
options: Fewer people will use trains to go to work.
More vehicles will use motorways at busy times.
Motorways would become a public good.
The costs of many businesses will increase.

questions.questionText: Carrots and potatoes are grown using the same factors of production. Figure X shows the demand (DC) and supply (SC) curves for carrots. Figure Y shows the demand (DP) and supply (SP) curves for potatoes. A change in people’s preferences shifts the demand for carrots from DC1 to DC2. As a result, the supply of potatoes shifts from SP1 to SP2. Which one of the following statements correctly explains the changes shown in Figures X and Y?
options: The demand curve for carrots shifts due to the rationing function of prices
The price of carrots increases because carrots and potatoes are in derived demand
The price of potatoes increases because potatoes and carrots are in joint supply
The supply curve for potatoes shifts due to the incentive function of prices

questions.questionText: Explain how the price mechanism allocates resources in a market economy.
The price mechanism allocates resources by
options: allowing prices to rise and ration demand when there is a surplus in the production of a good.
preventing firms with monopoly power from exploiting consumers and charging a price above the competitive price.
setting prices to ensure that the opportunity cost of producing a good is less than its social cost.
setting relative prices to determine the quantity of factors of production used in producing each good.

questions.questionText: Extract C (lines 14–15) states that ‘Rising prices will eventually also force builders in developing countries to explore alternatives to sand.’ Use the extracts and your knowledge of economics to assess the view that the increasing scarcity of sand is a problem best solved by market forces, rather than through government intervention.
The following diagram shows demand and supply in the market for roses. The demand for roses shifts from D1 to D2. Other things remaining the same, it can be concluded that
options: monopoly suppliers have pushed up the price of roses.
the higher price of roses will cause demand to fall back to D1.
the income elasticity of demand for roses is positive.
there is greater incentive to supply roses.

questions.questionText: One way to allocate road space in a congested city would be to charge drivers to use the roads. One reason why this policy is likely to result in a more efficient allocation of resources is because
options: incentives to build new roads would be higher.
only higher income drivers would choose to use the roads.
road use would be rationed to drivers who benefit from it the most.
the government would raise a large amount of revenue from drivers.

questions.questionText: In a free market economy, the economic problem of what goods should be produced is usually solved by
options: consumers expressing their tastes and preferences in their pattern of spending.
households completing business surveys to reveal their preferred products.
firms planning their activities to meet production targets set by government.
entrepreneurs producing their own goods to satisfy their own needs and wants.

questions.questionText: An increase in the world market price of wheat, following a series of poor harvests, leading to falling sales is an example of
options: market failure due to an externality in production.
government failure to support agricultural markets.
scarcity caused by high prices.
the rationing function of price.
